data.title: Cloudtech Achieves the AWS Data Competency
data.description:
Cloudtech Achieves the AWS Data Competency

Cloudtech Achieves the AWS Data Competency

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cloudtech Inc., a cloud and AI services company for small and mid-sized businesses, today announced that it has achieved the AWS Data Competency in the Analytics and Database categories. This designation recognizes Cloudtech for its demonstrated expertise delivering unified data architectures on Amazon Web Services (AWS), helping customers build the data foundations that power modern analytics and AI workloads.

Achieving the AWS Data Competency differentiates Cloudtech as a member of the AWS Partner Network (APN) with deep technical proficiency and proven customer success delivering data solutions on AWS. The Data Competency validates partners across the full data lifecycle, from databases and analytics to streaming, data engineering and AI-ready foundations, reflecting how customers build and modernize their data architectures.

About the AWS Data Competency Categories

  • Analytics: Design, build, and operate analytics solutions that unlock business intelligence and data-driven decision-making, leveraging services such as Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon Kinesis, Amazon MSK, and open-format data lakes on Apache Iceberg.
  • Database: Migrate, modernize, and manage production database workloads on AWS, spanning relational engines (Amazon RDS, Amazon Aurora) NoSQL and purpose-built databases (Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon DocumentDB, Amazon Neptune, Amazon ElastiCache, Amazon MemoryDB), and the full spectrum of operational disciplines from HA/DR architecture to performance optimization.

Executive Quote

"Cloudtech is proud to achieve the AWS Data Competency in the Analytics and Database categories," said Kamran Adil, CEO of Cloudtech. "For most small and mid-sized businesses, data is the difference between an AI pilot and AI that actually runs the business. This achievement reflects the work our team does every day to help customers organize, modernize and put their data to work on AWS, so they can move from AI ideas to real outcomes."

About the AWS Competency Program

AWS is enabling scalable, flexible, and cost-effective solutions from startups to global enterprises. To support the seamless integration and deployment of these solutions, the AWS Competency Program helps customers identify AWS Partners with deep industry experience and expertise across industries, use cases, and workloads to help grow their business.

About Cloudtech's Data Solutions

Cloudtech helps growing businesses get their data ready for AI. Its team migrates customers off legacy databases, modernizes their data architecture, and builds analytics and data foundations on AWS using services such as Amazon Aurora, Amazon RDS and Amazon Redshift to support Conversational AI and Generative AI. Engagements are delivered through fixed-price, defined-scope projects, so customers know the cost, deliverables, and timeline before work begins.

About Cloudtech

Cloudtech is an AWS Advanced Tier Services Partner and AWS SMB Competency Partner specializing in cloud migration, modernization, and AI for small and mid-sized businesses. Cloudtech helps growing companies move off legacy systems, modernize their applications and data on AWS, optimize cloud spend, and deploy Conversational AI and Generative AI, all built and delivered on AWS through fixed-price, defined-scope engagements. Learn more at cloudtech.com.

data.title: ADS-TEC Energy Secures Repeat Order from German Utility SWLB for Large-Scale Battery Storage Systems
data.description:
ADS-TEC Energy Secures Repeat Order from German Utility SWLB for Large-Scale Battery Storage Systems

Delivery of an ADS-TEC Energy BESS5000 battery storage system to German municipal utility Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg-Kornwestheim (SWLB). Following its successful commissioning, SWLB has ordered two additional systems with a combined capacity of 10 MWh

  • Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg-Kornwestheim (SWLB) places repeat order for two additional ADS-TEC Energy battery storage systems with a combined capacity of 10 megawatt-hours
  • The new systems will increase flexibility in the local power grid and support the development of a resilient, decentralized energy infrastructure
  • Battery storage technology developed and integrated in Germany

ADS-TEC Energy has secured a repeat order from German municipal utility Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg-Kornwestheim (SWLB) for two additional battery energy storage systems. The two BESS5000 systems have a combined capacity of 10 megawatt-hours and will be installed at the Reuteallee site in Ludwigsburg. Commissioning is scheduled for summer 2027.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119970868/en/

Delivery of an ADS-TEC Energy BESS5000 battery storage system.

Only about a year ago, SWLB placed an order with ADS-TEC Energy for a 5-megawatt-hour battery storage system, which is now operational at the utility's wood-fired combined heat and power plant in Ludwigsburg. The new order builds on the successful collaboration between the two companies.

German Battery Storage Technology for Municipal Energy Infrastructure

SWLB is pursuing a decentralized energy storage strategy, deploying multiple battery storage systems across its service area. The systems are designed to facilitate the integration of renewable energy, reduce strain on the power grid and create additional opportunities to participate in energy markets.

ADS-TEC Energy develops its battery storage technology in Germany and integrates the key technical components into a precisely matched overall system.

Michael Rudloff, COO of ADS-TEC Energy, comments: "We are pleased that SWLB has once again placed its trust in us and that we are continuing our successful collaboration. When building a decentralized energy storage infrastructure, it is essential that individual systems operate reliably and integrate seamlessly into existing systems. This is where we contribute our many years of experience in developing and integrating battery storage systems. The project shows that, in this area of critical infrastructure, local partnerships lead to effective solutions."

Sebastian Hess, Strategy and Corporate Development at Stadtwerke Ludwigsburg, adds: "The additional storage systems are a key component for a future-ready energy infrastructure and support the expansion of renewable energy in the region. By participating in the balancing market, we also aim to contribute to grid stability."

About ADS-TEC Energy

Building on more than 15 years of experience with lithium-ion technologies, ADS-TEC Energy develops and manufactures battery storage solutions and fast-charging systems, including their energy management systems.

Headquartered in Nürtingen, Germany, the company supports industrial companies, energy utilities and mobility providers in implementing modern energy solutions.

For more information, visit: www.ads-tec-energy.com.

data.title: My wife pays thousands for her family to visit us in New York. How can I ask her to choose between them and me?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night'

"I feel that some of her family members have come to take advantage of that generosity." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My wife and I have a wonderful marriage, but there is one recurring issue that has become a significant source of frustration for me. While my wife is an exceptionally generous and giving person, I feel that some of her family members have come to take advantage of that generosity.

Several of her relatives regularly want to visit us in New York, traveling from Argentina. Given the long journey, these visits typically last around two weeks. Some of her nieces, nephews and siblings expect to visit every year.

The problem is that we live in a Manhattan apartment with limited space, and hosting guests for extended periods is a significant imposition on our daily routines, privacy and overall quality of life. Now that we also have a baby, the logistical and personal challenges are even greater.

My wife is extremely devoted to her family and, for whatever reason, seems to have difficulty saying no to their requests. I've gently raised my concerns several times, explaining that we simply don't have the space to accommodate so many guests.

Many of her relatives have limited financial means, so my wife often ends up covering not only their flights and accommodations, but also airport transportation, meals, entertainment and other expenses.

Don't miss: My older brother, who has no children, cut our only sister out of his will. I'll get everything instead. Do I tell her?

Space constraints

While I appreciate that this addresses some of the space constraints, it creates a separate issue: the considerable financial burden. Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night, and the total cost of these visits can easily run into several thousand dollars.

Although my wife has her own money, these expenditures still have meaningful opportunity costs for our family. We have substantial financial priorities, including the high cost of childcare in New York City, saving toward purchasing a home and planning for our son's education.

It's also worth noting that we already travel to Argentina every year to visit her family. So it's not as though declining to host relatives in New York would prevent us from maintaining close relationships with them or spending time together.

I love my wife and I genuinely admire her generosity and commitment to her family. However, I'm increasingly feeling that her relatives' expectations are being prioritized over my comfort in our own home, our privacy and our family's financial goals.

I'm concerned that if this continues, my frustration will turn into resentment and undermine what is otherwise an excellent marriage. How can I establish reasonable boundaries? I don't want my wife to feel that I'm asking her to choose between me and her family.

The Husband

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her relatives, issues that might be rooted in her upbringing and culture.

Dear Husband,

When words fail to change bad habits, enlist a pen and paper.

This is a domestic as well as a financial problem. Your wife is spending money in isolation and without keeping your overall financial goals in mind. You probably are too, perhaps in smaller ways. This bad habit, which only appears to be getting worse, needs to be broken.

The only way to accomplish this is to show her how much money these trips are costing your family, in real terms, as you also pay for childcare and rent, save for emergencies and your child's schooling and college education, and put money aside to buy a home.

Of course, making it personal will only get you both mired in hurt feelings and defensiveness, so you need to take her family out of the equation as much as possible and revisit your marriage vows - your pact to respect and honor each other.

You can have these conversations alone, or with the help of a financial adviser or counselor. I suggest the latter. A mediator can help you articulate your concerns, frame your questions as "I feel ..." rather than "You are ..." and prevent you from hurting each other's feelings.

Ultimately, you need to formulate a family policy rather than take potshots at your wife's family. You have reached a stage in your married life when you are working toward tangible financial goals, and spending thousands of dollars on third parties compromises that.

A financial therapist could help to field your concerns.

Emphasize your shared responsibility and the importance of working as a team. Hosting relatives every year impinges on your privacy and ability to relax in your own home, disrupts your daily routines and makes your responsibilities as new parents more challenging.

Eventually, your wife will have to find the words to say no to people, her family included. It's not always easy, but after you do it once, it gets easier. Given that she has set an unhealthy precedent, this conversation can start with a soft no - and the truth.

She can tell her family: "This year is impossible for us to host. We no longer have room. We have a young child and a lot of family and work commitments." For what it's worth, there's also a difference between relatives visiting your city and crashing at your place.

I feel confident that facing up to the reality of your financial situation will encourage your wife to stop spending money meant for your little family on visiting relatives. Hotels, theater tickets and meals all add up, and something is wrong if her family members all expect the royal treatment.

Any expenditure over $1,000 should have veto power.

Facing that reality means making big decisions together - and spending thousands of dollars a year on visiting relatives is categorically a big decision, even if it seems like it's actually lots of small acts of generosity. Any expenditure over $1,000 should be discussed and agreed upon.

Many couples have a "mutual veto" on a large purchase. Some have a dollar cap, the size of which depends on their income. Unless there are two yes votes, the veto kicks in. But a dollar cap of $1,000 doesn't mean you can spend $999 each on a bunch of relatives.

Finally, many couples have "yours, mine and ours" accounts. They have a joint account for shared bills, savings and vacation money, and smaller personal checking accounts for guilt-free "mad money" splurges. But everything is accounted for in the family ledger.

At the root of this problem is why your wife feels obliged to host her relatives. Our relationship with money is emotional and, although we probably don't like to acknowledge it, less logical than we might imagine. She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her family.

A financial therapist could help explore why your wife feels such a strong sense of familial duty, which may be rooted in her upbringing and culture. She may even feel guilty about having achieved a more financially comfortable life than her relatives.

Whatever the reason behind it, the open-house era of hosting relatives should come to a close.

Related: 'The selling agent is long dead': My $250,000 term life-insurance policy costs $2,000 a month. I'm 80. Is it time to ditch it?

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

data.title: Philadelphia Area Manufacturing Activity Fell in November
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

Manufacturing activity in the Philadelphia area fell in November to a six-month low, according to a survey from the Philly Fed.

In the reserve bank's manufacturing business outlook survey, the current-activity index decreased to 6.3 in November from 20.9 in October. A reading above zero indicates an increase in business activity. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a reading of 18.

The current new orders index dropped five points to -0.4, its lowest reading since May and the index's fourth consecutive decline, the report said. The shipments index rose 10 points to 25.7, offsetting most of the previous month's decline.

The prices paid index rose to 58.2, its highest reading since April. The current prices received index increased seven points to 47, its highest reading since June 2022.

The employment index rose, continuing to suggest overall gains in employment.

The survey covers businesses in the Philly Fed's district, which includes Delaware and parts of eastern Pennsylvania and southern New Jersey.

data.title: Google turns to a volcano and rock-melting technology in a wild new bid to power AI
data.description:
By Claudia Assis

Google's agreement with Quaise is 'a bet on a first-of-a-kind technology,' according to a Bernstein analyst

Companies like Google are getting creative as AI fuels an energy crunch.

Google just gave a multimillion-dollar vote of confidence on an data-center power technology involving a volcano in Oregon, a gyrotron and melting rock.

It may sound far-fetched, but Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google is hoping to reap the benefits of that power purchase agreement as soon as 2030. This underscores how Big Tech companies are searching high and low for electricity to supply their data centers, preferably through clean energy, off-grid, or both, and as the industry seeks to ward off the criticism that data centers are power hogs contributing to higher electricity bills.

Project Obsidian is a super-hot-rock geothermal project on the flank of the Newberry Volcano in central Oregon. Google on Tuesday signed a power purchase agreement for 50 megawatts with startup Quaise Energy to support Google's existing data-center operations in The Dalles, Ore. Quaise has oilfield-services company Nabors (NBR) as one of its backers.

Don't miss: An overlooked energy source could solve AI's power crunch - and these 2 stocks are prime plays

Neither party disclosed the deal's price or structure, but it is reportedly above $500 million, according to the Wall Street Journal.

"The size of the deal puts this as a bet on a first-of-a-kind technology," analysts at Bernstein said in a note.

It's good news for next-generation geothermal energy, "which we continue to believe is the only way for geothermal energy to reach scale," they said.

Geothermal technology uses the Earth's heat to power turbines that create renewable electricity. Crucially, it produces clean energy around the clock, unlike solar and wind power.

Behind the hunger for power and data centers is unabated demand for AI computing.

The latest technology bet is a gyratron, a tool used in fusion research that has been repurposed to melt rock with millimeter waves rather than grinding through it. That way geothermal wells can go deeper and hotter than what would be possible using drill bits.

Quaise's field record is "thin so far," the Bernstein analysts said, with shallow demonstration holes rather than actual wells produced, which is why Project Obsidian is "effectively the proof point for the company," they said.

Geothermal energy itself got a big vote of confidence earlier this month, when analysts at Morgan Stanley highlighted some of the latest leaps in geothermal power generation - including some of the same tools that made the U.S. oil-and-gas shale revolution possible.

Don't miss: Nvidia's booming demand is 'hard to ignore,' but these four questions loom over the stock

-Claudia Assis

data.title: Thermo Bond Expands Critical Infrastructure Business to Support Distributed Computing Development
data.description:
Thermo Bond Expands Critical Infrastructure Business to Support Distributed Computing Development

Steven Tims promoted to president as company scales its factory-built infrastructure model for new infrastructure demand

Thermo Bond, a 39-year-old manufacturer of critical infrastructure, today expanded its business to provide the precast concrete semi-permanent structures and campuses needed to deploy and scale distributed computing. Steven Tims has been promoted to president to lead the company and its growth in the new market alongside its established telecom, fiber and utility business.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119899492/en/

Thermo Bond Solutions' Edge Vault Unit being lifted into place.

As part of this change, all Thermo Bond divisions and product lines will now operate under the Thermo Bond Solutions name, bringing its mission-critical infrastructure experience, manufacturing capabilities and delivery model together under one organization.

At the center of the expansion is the Edge Vault, Thermo Bond’s patent-pending, factory-built concrete structure designed to house and protect computing equipment. Edge Vault Units can be deployed individually or combined into an Edge Vault Node or Edge Vault Campus, allowing developers and operators to add infrastructure in stages, expand capacity over time and plan around available power, land and site conditions. Thermo Bond builds the structures and campus infrastructure, while customers provide and operate the computing equipment inside.

“We see a real opportunity to take what Thermo Bond has done well for decades and build a new approach for how computing infrastructure can be developed today,” said Steven Tims, president of Thermo Bond Solutions. “Not every project needs to be one massive site. Our model gives developers a new option to put computing capacity closer to available power, scale it over time and build in a way that fits the communities around it.”

A Scalable Model for Distributed Infrastructure

Thermo Bond sees opportunity with developers evaluating individual sites as well as operators planning deployments across multiple locations. For customers responding to growing AI and other computing needs, the model can complement hyperscale development and gives customers the flexibility to build at a range of scales, from smaller modular deployments to larger campuses. Its repeatable, factory-built approach allows infrastructure to be deployed in stages rather than requiring an entire campus to be built at once, giving customers more flexibility to scale as computing needs grow and do so in a way that fits their business case and the communities where they operate.

The model also fits rural locations where land and power may be available outside traditional data center markets, while having less overall water and noise impact. Edge Vault’s cooling system uses a sealed loop filled once at commissioning, with no recurring water use, while sound-insulated chillers help reduce noise. Projects can be sized and expanded around local conditions and community interest, giving developers more options for where and how they deploy infrastructure.

Thermo Bond has nearly 700 team members across manufacturing operations in South Dakota and Indiana, with products deployed in 49 states. Over the coming months, its Brandon, South Dakota, facility will transition to Edge Vault production. The company will continue to serve its longtime telecom and utility customers at its other plant locations.

Leadership for Growth

Since joining Thermo Bond in 2025, Tims has led the company’s work to evaluate how its manufacturing capabilities can support the growing need for infrastructure to house and deploy computing capacity. As president, he will lead the overall company and strategy across Thermo Bond’s plants and product lines as the company prepares for growth in both its established and emerging markets. Previously, he was the chief operating officer (COO) of Viaflex and spent more than a decade at Raven Industries, where he held leadership roles across technology and manufacturing operations.

Paul Muth will serve as executive director, working alongside Tims and the leadership team on behalf of the Muth family, which owns Thermo Bond. Muth previously served as president of Muth Electric and brings operational experience to support the company as it ramps facilities and optimizes production.

“The buildings that protect our networks today are the same ones the next generation of infrastructure needs, built in more places and closer to where the power already is,” said Doug Muth, speaking on behalf of the Muth family ownership. “Our family is all in on that, and Steven has our full confidence to take the organization forward.”

To learn more about Thermo Bond Solutions and its Edge Vault line for deploying distributed computing infrastructure, visit: thermobond.com.

About Thermo Bond Solutions

Thermo Bond Solutions is a family-owned manufacturer of factory-built critical infrastructure for telecom, fiber, utility and distributed computing. For 39 years, the company has built and delivered infrastructure designed for durability, repeatable deployment and long-term growth across a range of sites and applications.

Thermo Bond has nearly 700 team members, manufacturing operations in South Dakota and Indiana, and products deployed in 49 states. The company is owned by the Muth family. Learn more: thermobond.com.

data.title: Google's New Gemini 4 Neon Joins Gemini 4 Argon at the Top of the DualEntry Accounting AI
data.description:
Google's New Gemini 4 Neon Joins Gemini 4 Argon at the Top of the DualEntry Accounting AI

Google's newly released Gemini 4 Neon got 91.1% of accounting tasks right on the DualEntry Accounting AI Benchmark, tying Google's Gemini 4 Argon for the highest score among 29 leading AI models tested.

Neon beat Argon on bank reconciliation (91.7% vs 75%) and on hard tasks (85.7% vs 82.1%). Argon was slightly more consistent (86.1% vs 85.1%) and cheaper per task.

Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is tied for third at 88.1% with Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 Flash and SpaceXAI's Grok 4.7. That puts Google's models first, second and tied for third on the benchmark, the strongest showing by any provider.

Key findings:

  • Gemini 4 Neon scored 91.1% overall, tied for first of 29 with Gemini 4 Argon
  • Google's models are first, second and tied for third: Neon and Argon at 91.1%, then Gemini 4 Carbon at 88.1%, level with GLM-5.3 Flash and Grok 4.7
  • It leads Anthropic's best model, Claude Fable 5.1 (85.1%), by 6.0 points, and OpenAI's best, GPT-6.2 Sol (84.2%), by 6.9 points
  • It scored 100% on transaction classification and financial reporting, and 91.7% on accounts receivable and bank reconciliation
  • It scored 85.7% on hard tasks (24 of 28), ahead of Argon's 82.1%, and 97.2% on medium tasks (35 of 36)
  • Its consistency score was 85.1%, compared with 86.1% for Gemini 4 Argon
  • It costs $0.174 per task ($52.76 for a full benchmark run), about 50% more than Gemini 4 Argon ($0.115), and averages 24.3 seconds per task
  • On bank reconciliation it scored 91.7%, 16.7 points ahead of Argon

Gemini 4 Neon was not the strongest model in every category. Its weakest result came in month-end close at 66.7% (8 of 12), where Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 led at 91.7% and Argon scored 83.3%.

"Google now has two models tied at the top of our benchmark, and both get nine in ten accounting tasks right," said Benedict Dohmen, co-founder of DualEntry. "For finance teams the question is no longer whether AI can do the work, but whether it gets the same answer every time, and that is what separates the leaders."

The DualEntry Accounting AI Benchmark tests models on 101 synthetic accounting cases across eight areas: transaction classification, journal entries, accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank reconciliation, financial reporting, month-end close, and accounting knowledge.

Each model completes the full benchmark three times from an identical test company with the same tools and instructions. Answers are checked against reference answers written in advance using fixed scoring rules rather than an AI grader. No customer data is used.

Full results for all 29 models, including accuracy, consistency, cost, response time, and performance by accounting area, are available at dualentry.com/benchmark.

About DualEntry

DualEntry is the agentic, AI-native ERP for mid-market finance teams. It brings the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, revenue recognition, multi-entity consolidation, and reporting into one platform, with AI agents that take on accounting work from data entry through close. Founded in 2024 and based in New York, DualEntry raised a $90 million Series A in 2025 from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and GV. Learn more at DualEntry.com.

Top Third-Party Logistics (3PL) Companies in the US for 2026

PR Newswire

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 19, 2026

An overview of providers serving DTC brands, multichannel retailers, specialized product categories and growing online businesses

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- E-commerce businesses selling in the United States rely on fulfillment partners to store inventory, process orders, coordinate shipping and manage returns. The right provider depends on factors such as product type, order volume, sales channels and delivery expectations. This industry overview examines six companies with different fulfillment models and service strengths.

The companies were selected based on publicly available information about US warehousing, ecommerce order processing, technology integrations, shipping options, returns and specialized capabilities. They are presented alphabetically, not as a ranking of performance.

  1. Cart.com operates a nationwide fulfillment network and supports omnichannel order processing across direct-to-consumer, wholesale, retail and B2B channels. Its services include picking, packing, shipping, inventory visibility, kitting, bundling and Amazon FBA preparation.

  2. Fulfillment Service provides warehousing and order fulfillment from its facility in Traverse City, Michigan. It serves businesses from startups to established merchants, with no order minimums or long-term contracts and integrations with more than 40 shopping carts and marketplaces.

  3. Lansil Global combines US order fulfillment with China-based sourcing and manufacturing support. Its network includes a 98,221-square-foot Shenzhen facility, a 106,624-square-foot Nevada warehouse and a 32,069-square-foot Pennsylvania facility, totaling more than 236,000 square feet. The company reported shipping more than 20 million parcels worldwide by the end of 2025. Its experience spans industries such as Beauty & Cosmetics, Electronics, Jewelry & Accessories, Health & Wellness, Fashion & Apparel, and Home & Kitchen. Services include inventory management, order processing, kitting and bundling, Amazon FBA preparation and global distribution.

  4. Red Stag Fulfillment focuses on large, heavy and bulky products that require specialized storage, handling and shipping. Its services cover direct-to-consumer parcel orders, pallet shipments, retail distribution, Amazon fulfillment, returns and kitting.

  5. ShipBob supports DTC and B2B fulfillment through a distributed network of fulfillment centers in the US and other markets. Its services include inventory placement, picking, packing, shipping, returns and integrations with ecommerce platforms and sales channels.

  6. ShipMonk combines fulfillment operations with proprietary technology for inventory and order management. It serves DTC, B2B and retail businesses and offers kitting, customization, returns processing and integrations with ecommerce platforms and marketplaces.

What Should Businesses Consider When Choosing a 3PL Partner?

Businesses should compare warehouse locations with customer demand and review receiving, storage, pick-and-pack, shipping and returns fees. Platform integrations, inventory visibility, product dimensions, seasonal capacity, service-level commitments and support availability also affect whether a 3PL provider fits a brand's operating needs.
